articles.summary: arXiv:2607.27251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformer-based surrogate models are increasingly used to replace expensive first-principles simulation in engineering design. articles.title: Regularizing modality contribution drift in multimodal continual learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.27260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal continual learning (MMCL) aims to learn emerging knowledge from multimodal data while preserving knowledge. To mitigate forgetting, current MMCL methods usually focus on cross-modal representation alignment or semantic similarity, but they overlook whether the relative contributions of individual modalities and their interactions remain stable across incremental tasks. We term this decision-level shift Modality Contribution Drift (MCD) and quantify it with the MCD score, which combines contribution-strength and relative-reliance change

articles.title: ZUNA1.1: A more flexible EEG foundation model for Denoising and Super-resolution
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.27308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce ZUNA1.1, a 380M-parameter diffusion autoencoder for flexible EEG signal reconstruction. ZUNA1.1 is capable of reconstructing variable length sequences of up to 30s, with an arbitrary number of EEG channels at arbitrary scalp locations, and can reconstruct arbitrary temporal intervals within channels in addition to reconstructing entire channels. We demonstrate that ZUNA1.1 performs at least on par with our earlier ZUNA1 model, while being far more flexible and capable of handling a wide range of reconstruction tasks. ZUNA1.1 contin

articles.title: What if the brain does not create consciousness?
articles.summary: Christof Koch is taking on one of science’s deepest mysteries: how the brain creates conscious experience, or whether it creates it at all. He argues that materialism has yet to solve this “hard problem” and will explore puzzling phenomena such as near-death experiences and terminal lucidity. His work points toward the possibility that consciousness may be woven into reality itself.

articles.title: Creatine supplements show potential for managing major depressive disorder
articles.summary: A new systematic review suggests that creatine monohydrate, a popular supplement for athletes, might help treat major depressive disorder. Evidence indicates that combining creatine with standard antidepressants or talk therapy tends to improve depressive symptoms in adults.

articles.title: Even More Deception: Objective Misalignment in Mixed-Motive LLM Multi-Agent Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.26120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs)-powered multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed in mixed-motive environments, where agents operate under asymmetric information and strategic deception due to conflicting or hidden objectives. In these settings, misalignment with collective goals becomes a central concern. We propose a novel framework for evaluating objective misalignment using the social deduction game Werewolf, modifying the objective of a single agent while preserving its assigned role. Across LLMs from four different model families and sizes

articles.title: ClinLens: Towards Long-Horizon Coding Agents for Longitudinal Multimodal Clinical Data Science
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.26155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical data-science agents must transform heterogeneous longitudinal records into auditable analyses, yet existing benchmarks largely isolate medical question answering, structured-table reasoning, or generic scientific repositories. We introduce CLINLENS, a benchmark of 200 executable tasks over five linked MIMIC resources spanning structured electronic health records, notes, electrocardiograms, chest radiographs, and echocardiograms. A 4 x 5 taxonomy crosses four patient-time scopes with five analysis capabilities. Program-first reverse synth

articles.title: When benchmark inferences do not compose: Projectibility in AI evaluation
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.26159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An AI benchmark result rarely reaches a consequential claim in one step. Evaluators generalize it to further cases, interpret it as evidence of capability, extrapolate it to new tasks, transport it to another system or site, and combine it with assumptions about human review and downstream consequences. Validity-centred approaches require evidence for each claim. This paper identifies a further epistemic problem: warranted links don't automatically make a warranted chain. articles.title: New study reveals an unexpected difference between casual and compulsive pornography viewers
articles.summary: A new analysis of over 100,000 individuals reveals a notable link between watching recreational pornography and engaging in interactive online sexual behaviors like sexting. The research highlights the nuanced psychological boundaries dividing casual viewing from solitary compulsive habits.
